newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Dlr/mark upbreak targets 1.7120 and highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dlr/mark upbreak targets 1.7120 and highs.

text.p: The dollar has broken up through the 1.70 marks barrier, and is now set to test the recent high of 1.7120 and beyond, chart watchers said.

"This morning it's a question of 'where can we buy?'," said Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management UK. "Dollar/mark is heading towards 1.7120, I think as part of a bigger test of the highs at 1.7300/85."
The dollar hit 1.7389 marks on April 28, its strongest level since February 1994, and has since shimmied down into a lower trading band which made a low of 1.6680 on May 12.
It was trading at 1.7043/48 marks at 0725 GMT, little changed from late Tuesday's European level of 1.7045/50.

Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London, said the break higher should set the stage for a potential rally above 1.7380 if this was a bull flag breakout -- which would set a minimum goal of 1.7665 marks.
But some intraday pullback threatens first.

"For today, watch for some consolidative pressures as hourly momentum heads lower from overbought," he said. "This could see the dollar pressed towards 1.7020/00 and potentially the 1.6980 trendline and old resistance."
The 1.6980 area must hold to convince of further dollar gains later on, Celaya said.
The U.S. currency continues to grind higher against the yen, and analysts said a break of the psychological 117 level -- which it glanced overnight -- was now on the cards.
"I think it's tired, but it is still in an uptrend, and the next target will be 118," said Matts at Capital Management.
Trendline resistance cuts in around 118 yen, drawn from the 111.88 low the dollar hit on May 20.
The dollar stood at 116.25/35 yen at 0743 GMT versus Tuesday's European close of 116.51/56.
On the downside, support slices in at yesterday's lows near 115.80, with congestion at 115.50/30 and then the round-figure 115.00 beneath there, analysts said.
-- RSI - 14 day: Dollar/mark: 51 pct, Dollar/yen: 36 pct
